sentences.text:
2. Heard Sri G.G. Chagashetti, learned counsel appearing for the appellant and Sri Ganesh S.
Kalburgi, learned counsel appearing for respondent Nos.1(b) to 1(h), 2, 3, 4(a) to 4(i), 5 (b), 5(c) and 5(d).
3. The plaintiffs instituted suit in O.S.No.1/2009 seeking partition and separate possession.

The Trial Court partly decreed the suit of the plaintiffs holding that the plaintiffs and defendants are entitled for partition and NC: 2024:KHC-K:4681 separate share in the suit schedule properties as prayed and preliminary decree was directed to be drawn accordingly.
The plaintiffs instituted FDP No.11/2014 before the concerned Court under Order XX Rule 18 read with Section 54 of CPC.

entities.text: Order XX Rule 18 read with Section 54
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: The petition filed by the plaintiffs came to be dismissed holding that the request of the petitioners to modify the share of the petitioners is beyond the scope of the present final decree proceedings and liberty was granted to the petitioners-plaintiffs to challenge the decree passed in O.S.No.1/2009 by filing regular appeal before the first appellate Court.
The plaintiffs preferred R.A.No.11/2021 against the judgment and order in FDP No.11/2014 before the first appellate Court.

The first appellate Court allowed the appeal and held that the appellants are entitled for 2/10th share and the legal representatives of petitioner Nos.4 to 5 are entitled for 1/10th share each, respondent No.1 is entitled for remaining 2/10th share in the suit schedule properties excluding three storied building existing in the land bearing Sy.No.95 situated at Aland Colony, Kalaburagi.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:4681 Aggrieved by the quantum of share, defendant No.1 is before this Court.

4. The ground made out by the appellant is that in FDP No.11/2014, a third party one Sameeruddin had filed I.A. under Order XXI Rules 97 and 101 read with Section 151 of CPC seeking to decide his right and interest in the suit schedule properties and the said application has been rejected.

The grounds urged in the appeal papers are more pertaining to the rejection of the I.A. of the third party and the substantial question of law raised by the appellant is that "whether the lower appellate Court is justified in law in rectifying and modifying the preliminary decree passed in O.S.No.1/2009 though the very modification decree is pending consideration in FDP No.11/2014?"
5.

Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the respondents justifies the judgment and decree of the first appellate Court and contended that the Trial Court in the final decree proceedings ought to have specified the NC: 2024:KHC-K:4681 shares of the parties as they are the Mohammedans and the share to be quantified are fixed,
instead of following the said procedure, the final decree Court directed the plaintiffs to file appeal against O.S.No.1/2009.

Learned counsel submits that the plaintiffs are not aggrieved by the judgment and decree passed in O.S.No.1/2009, but the FDP was filed only for quantifying the shares in respect of the suit schedule properties.

The undisputed fact is that O.S.No.1/2009 came to be decreed in part which reads as under:
"The suit filed by the plaintiffs is hereby partly decreed.
It is hereby decreed that,
plaintiffs and defendants are entitled to get partition and separate share in the suit schedule properties as prayed in the plaint.

But, claiming the share by the plaintiffs in the compensation amount in the Land Acquisition Act is hereby rejected.
Draw preliminary decree accordingly."
NC: 2024:KHC-K:4681 7.
The judgment and decree in O.S. No.1/2009 has attained finality and the entitlement of a legitimate share of the plaintiffs and defendants.
8. FDP No.11/2014 was preferred by the plaintiffs under Order XX Rule 18 read with Section 54 CPC.

entities.text: Order XX Rule 18 read with Section 54
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text:
The FDP Court by the order dated 04.03.2020 passed the following order:
"The petition filed by the petitioners U/o. 20 rule 18 R/w section 54 of CPC is hereby dismissed as same is not maintainable.

Claim of petitioners that, another preliminary decree can be drawn by modifying share of sharers as per their personal Law as mentioned in their objection to Commissioner Report dated 28.02.2019, wherein petitioners requested to modify share of these petitioners together as 8/11th share, share of respondent No.1 as 2/11th share and share of respondent No.2 as 1/11th share is beyond scope of present Final Decree Proceedings.

Only option left to petitioners is to challenge Decree passed in OS No.1/2009 by filing Regular Appeal before Appellate Court."
- 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:4681 9.

The plaintiffs sought modification of the preliminary decree or to pass another preliminary decree by filing necessary application before the Trial Court, contending that the specific shares of the parties were not determined in accordance with their personal law and there would be no impediment to the Trial Court to modify the earlier preliminary decree or to pass another preliminary decree under I.A. in accordance with law.

10. The parties herein are governed by Mohammedan law and there is no birth right in the suit properties during the lifetime of Mohd. Aleemuddin and after the death of the plaintiff's father, the parties to the suit, i.e., the legal representatives who are the petitioners Shaban Begum vs Saleemoddin And Ors on 8 July, 2024

sentences.text: Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59858340/
6 -plaintiffs being the sharers under the law of inheritance are entitled for share.

The shares under the Mohammedan law are fixed and the petitioners, being the sons, are entitled for equal share, i.e.,
2/10th share and the legal representatives of petitioner Nos.4 and 5 are entitled for 1/10th

The first appellate Court, while re-assessing the - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:4681 entire oral and documentary evidence, observed that, when the petitioners approached the Trial Court with the prayer to modify the preliminary decree passed in O.S.No.1/2009 the application ought to have been considered by the Trial Court.
The first appellate Court held that the Trial Court was not justified in declining specific shares to the parties under personal law by modifying the preliminary decree as sought for.
The entitlement of shares to the plaintiffs and defendants in the partition suit has already attained finality.
What remained before the courts, more particularly the final decree court, was the quantification of share, which the final decree Court ought to have done.
The first appellate Court has rightly re-appreciated and held that the preliminary decree passed needs to be modified.
The judgment and decree of the first appellate Court do not warrant any interference and no substantial questions of law arise for consideration in the present appeal.

Accordingly, this Court pass the following:
ORDER (i) The Regular Second Appeal is hereby dismissed.
(ii) The judgment and decree of the courts below stands confirmed.
